newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil govt's bank merger programme seen near end.
newsitem.headline: Brazil govt's bank merger programme seen near end.

text.p: The Brazilian government's program to help mergers and acquisitions in the banking sector is close to ending but will probably continue into next year, Central Bank president Gustavo Loyola said.
A December 31 deadline applies only to an incentive allowing banks to discount costs involved in the takeover of other institutions from their corporate tax payments, he told Reuters.

Reports have said the government intended to extinguish PROER, as the programme is known by its Portuguese acronym, by the end of the year. But Loyola said special credit lines to help mergers and acquisitions would not be stopped immediately.
"PROER is not set to end on December 31...although I personally believe we're practically at the end," Loyola said.

"PROER could end. The process of consolidating (banks) doesn't depend on it. PROER helped the government avoid a crisis of confidence in the system. Once the main problems have been eliminated, it can be done away with," he said.

Since its inception in November 1995, PROER has granted over 14 billion reais to banks buying up other financial institutions. The money is released from reserve requirement funds the banks must deposit with the Central Bank.
Loyola declined to comment on the state of negotiations over the future of Bamerindus, Brazil's fourth largest private bank which has been the target of takeover speculation for months.
